findings.evidence: Plan-v1 cases[M70-ORIGINAL-DEFECT].assertions[1] requires genuine-stall controls to pass under restored awaited-context observation; gates[M70-MUTATION].method explicitly selects unchanged context-stall-1/2 and expected requires them to pass. These fixtures specifically require the candidate worker-wide reset: test/replay_timeout_controller_test.cpp:181-195 releases job0 in context0, waits for its real completion while context2 stays incomplete, then advances the dispatcher clock by1.5s. Lines197-200 withhold every other job and advance by1.999s then1.001s. The production deadline is armed before waiting (cli/fossilize_replay.cpp:1013-1015), reset only when the observed counter changes (1032-1034), and expires at elapsed>=threshold (cli/replay_timeout.hpp:44-47). Candidate reset at+1.5s gives no trigger at+3.499s and a3s trigger at+4.5s. Restoring completed_count[2] observation cannot reset at context0 completion, so it triggers at+3.499s after only two adapter steps. Unchanged assertions require elapsed3000000000ns, steps3/signal_order1 and one real completion (fixture236-241,620-625,631). Thus these are valid progress-then-stall candidate regressions, but cannot pass under the original rule. The host libstdc++13 condition_variable wait_until checks steady_clock after the wrapped wait; its predicate does not convert context0 completion into context2 progress.
